nodes.rationale: The coordinate orders are partial and share only 0.3% of pairs, so no single order relates most pairs; but every pair has a meet and a join, so the interval is total where the order is partial. nodes.norm_label: the negative results are the strongest chapters
nodes.rationale: They are negative because a nothing was defined rather than discarded — 1,061 perturbation bounds from a bracket's non-failure, an impossibility proof from a fruitless search.

nodes.label: Nothing is something definable
nodes.rationale: A null is still definable; its definition comes not from inside the cell but from an observation made outside it — the exchange that made the object known at all.

nodes.label: Protocol §2.14 — compute, then write
nodes.rationale: Written because the failure of concluding before reading output was measured rather than deplored; it happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so care cannot fix it.

nodes.label: Redundancy of paths, not redundancy of care
nodes.norm_label: redundancy of paths, not redundancy of care
nodes.rationale: The protocols were written and broken by the same person in one week; what saved the results is that four different things were looking and not at the same thing.

nodes.label: The error class no structure catches
nodes.norm_label: the error class no structure catches
nodes.rationale: A guard returned a null read as false; every relation checked out and every number agreed while all of it was wrong, because the arithmetic stayed consistent with corrupted input. Only being asked to look again reached it.

nodes.label: The register — 1,629 entries in three populations
nodes.norm_label: the register — 1,629 entries in three populations
nodes.rationale: The register is evidence not that the work was error-prone but that errors were converted into structure.

nodes.label: The identity w = V·e
nodes.rationale: A relation that data cannot violate is not empty — it defends the derivation that produced it, checking that a quantity reached one way agrees with the same quantity reached another way.

nodes.label: The wrong nuclear charge in Chapter 16
nodes.norm_label: the wrong nuclear charge in chapter 16
nodes.rationale: The bracket held 56 of 56 and could not notice because Z cancels from the containment test; two quantities the method never uses were loud at once — the object found the error because it carried more than it needed.

nodes.label: How to read this register
nodes.rationale: The register is the working record the five compendia are distilled from: it argues, reverses itself and keeps the reversals; the compendia answer, this is where the answers were got.

nodes.rationale: Research figure. Caption: 'Λ8 · eight coordinates · seven constraints · a caterpillar with 2S pendant at k'. nodes.label: Caterpillar topology (spine plus one pendant)
nodes.rationale: Calling the constraint graph a caterpillar is the load-bearing claim of the figure: a caterpillar is a tree whose non-leaf nodes form a path, so the whole of Λ8 can be solved by a single sweep along the spine n → ℓ → k → q → g ← f ← e with 2S hanging off k. No cycles means no simultaneous solve is required.

nodes.label: Figure I2 — The Index Landscape (every index this work builds or draws)
nodes.community_name: extracted: Figure I2 — The Index Landscape (every
nodes.norm_label: figure i2 — the index landscape (every index this work builds or draws)
nodes.rationale: Log-log scatter census of every index in the corpus: x = number of cells (10^1 to 10^5), y = E + 1 (defect, 10^0 to 10^2). Two plotted classes distinguished by glyph: blue open circle = TRANSITION index (has a time column), red open square = STATE index (cannot have one). The figure exists to show the whole population at once so that defect can be read against size rather than argued case by case.

nodes.label: Defect is not a function of index size
nodes.community_name: extracted: Figure I2 — The Index Landscape (every
nodes.norm_label: defect is not a function of index size
nodes.rationale: The result the figure demonstrates. The scatter shows no trend across four decades of size: the smallest indexes ('the protocols' at roughly 19 cells) carry the largest defect (E near 100), while the largest (Lambda-13 at roughly 6x10^4 cells) sits at zero, and Lambda-10 and the violation index sit at nearly identical size on opposite ends of the defect axis. Method: plot every index the work builds or draws on one log-log axis, marked by class, and let the absence of a trend line be the argument — defect is a property of what an index closes, not of how many cells it has.

nodes.label: beta_nl per-sibling destabilisation as a shell constant
nodes.community_name: recovered: Shell-ordered under-binding of the loc
nodes.norm_label: beta_nl per-sibling destabilisation as a shell constant
nodes.rationale: indirect / N_sib is constant within a shell (beta_4f = 0.0044 Ha/sibling to 1e-4 on four rows, beta_3d ~ 0.007); recorded as an OUTPUT read off the run, not fitted, and still owed a frozen-orbital check.

nodes.label: The shells share an ADDITIVE ~0.02 Ha shallowness, not a fractional SR error
nodes.community_name: recovered: Shell-ordered under-binding of the loc
nodes.norm_label: the shells share an additive ~0.02 ha shallowness, not a fractional sr error
nodes.rationale: The same 0.02 is 10 % of the 4f indirect SR term and ~90 % of the 5d one, which rules out a common fractional error and points all three checks at one place: the local exchange kernel on a localised half-occupied entrant against a contracted core.

nodes.label: SIC does not commute with SR on 4f (PC1 qualified)
nodes.community_name: recovered: Shell-ordered under-binding of the loc
nodes.norm_label: sic does not commute with sr on 4f (pc1 qualified)
nodes.rationale: SR contracts 4f so each sibling's V_SIC on the entrant grows and beta_4f grows, adding +0.011..+0.014 to the 4f SIC shift while the direct term keeps its sign; entered per R 1449 as a qualification of the earlier reach claim rather than a silent drop.

nodes.label: Shell-ordered under-binding of the local-exchange spin-polarised TS object (s < f ~ d, 0.003-0.03 Ha)
nodes.community_name: recovered: Shell-ordered under-binding of the loc
nodes.norm_label: shell-ordered under-binding of the local-exchange spin-polarised ts object (s < f ~ d, 0.003-0.03 ha)
nodes.rationale: Present nonrelativistically and not created by the SR step; on 5d it merely happens to be the size of the SR shift, which is why an earlier bridge read it as an SR-step edge. Interpretation offered, not claimed: the signature of local exchange on a localised half-occupied orbital.

nodes.label: SIC shift ordered by channel filling, not by shell
nodes.community_name: recovered: Shell-ordered under-binding of the loc
nodes.norm_label: sic shift ordered by channel filling, not by shell
nodes.rationale: Read off the run and bound rather than fitted: an up-channel entrant with few siblings deepens 0.012-0.026, a half-filled up channel (Cr d5) gives zero, and a down-channel entrant turns positive as the channel fills. Named as the s17 mechanism (self-Hartree ~ f vs Dirac self-exchange ~ f^4/3 at f = 1/2) plus sibling relaxation, and flagged as a candidate DERIVABLE structure.

nodes.label: shift_SIC = direct(nl; Z) + beta_nl * N_sib
nodes.community_name: recovered: Shell-ordered under-binding of the loc
nodes.rationale: Derived structure with no constant chosen: direct is the entrant's own relaxed half-electron self-term, beta_nl the per-sibling destabilisation from each sibling's own V_SIC contracting it onto the entrant. Both are computable from the object with no input, so the law explains sign changes without a fit.

nodes.label: PZ6': the split is the entrant's spin (up-entrants inside, down-entrants outside)
nodes.community_name: recovered: Shell-ordered under-binding of the loc
nodes.norm_label: pz6': the split is the entrant's spin (up-entrants inside, down-entrants outside)
nodes.rationale: The spin-resolved potential v_dn = eps - (r_s/3)eps' - (1+zeta) d eps/d zeta is deeper than either bracket edge in a polarised background: the U/P bracket assumed one potential for both spins while the LSD functional does not. Stated after batch 1 and before batches 2-3 per R 1449, and read as what the bracket hid rather than a fault of the object.

nodes.norm_label: figure: the solid in silhouette (plan and side views)

nodes.label: Containment / bracket test (cells bracketed)
nodes.rationale: The pass/fail acceptance test counting how many cells are bracketed. It returns 4/4 for both Z = 1 and Z = 2, so it cannot separate the wrong charge from the right one — the panel is annotated 'the bracket cannot see it'.

nodes.label: Z = 2 (correct nuclear charge)
nodes.rationale: Under Z = 2 delta is essentially constant across n (about 1.308 down to 1.265), spread 0.04 — a flat delta is the mark of the correct charge.

nodes.label: Delta spread statistic
nodes.rationale: Scalar summary annotated on each series: max-minus-min of delta over the plotted n range. Reported as 2.48 for Z = 1 and 0.04 for Z = 2.

nodes.label: Helium-like series implied by Z = 2 (AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.rationale: AMBIGUOUS — the figure names no element. A correct Z = 2 with delta near 1.27 over n = 4..9 is consistent with a singly-ionised helium-like / two-charge core series, but the identification is inferred from the charge value alone and is not stated in the figure.

nodes.label: Nuclear charge Z
nodes.rationale: The parameter being tested. The figure contrasts a wrong assignment (Z = 1) against the correct one (Z = 2) for the same series.

nodes.label: Principal quantum number n (n = 4..9)
nodes.rationale: Shared x-axis of both delta panels; six plotted points at n = 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.

nodes.label: Quantum defect delta
nodes.rationale: The y-axis of both right-hand panels, plotted against principal quantum number n. Its constancy across n is the diagnostic quantity: delta is expected to be nearly n-independent when the charge is right.

nodes.label: spread 0.04 (Z = 2 series)
nodes.rationale: Annotation on the right panel. Delta runs from about 1.308 at n = 4 to about 1.265 at n = 9 on a magnified axis spanning 1.26 to 1.31 (endpoint values AMBIGUOUS — read off the axis).

nodes.label: spread 2.48 (Z = 1 series)
nodes.rationale: Annotation on the middle panel. Endpoints read approximately 2.65 at n = 4 and 5.15 at n = 9, consistent with a spread of 2.48 (endpoint values AMBIGUOUS — read off the axis, not stated numerically).

nodes.label: Z = 1 (wrong nuclear charge)
nodes.rationale: Under Z = 1 the inferred delta drifts monotonically upward with n (about 2.65 to 5.15 over n = 4..9), spread 2.48 — the signature of a mis-set charge.

nodes.label: Panel A — cells bracketed, 4/4 for both Z
nodes.norm_label: panel a — cells bracketed, 4/4 for both z
nodes.rationale: Grey bar chart, y-axis 'cells bracketed' 0..5, two identical bars at height 4 labelled 4/4 over categories Z = 1 and Z = 2.

nodes.label: Panel B — delta vs n under Z = 1 (red, rising)
nodes.norm_label: panel b — delta vs n under z = 1 (red, rising)
nodes.rationale: Red marker-and-line series, near-linear ascent, y-axis delta about 2.6 to 5.2.

nodes.label: Panel C — delta vs n under Z = 2 (blue, flat/decaying)
nodes.norm_label: panel c — delta vs n under z = 2 (blue, flat/decaying)
nodes.rationale: Blue marker-and-line series flattening toward an asymptote near 1.265 on a magnified axis; the residual downward curvature is a convergent tail, not a drift.

nodes.label: Figure 9.1 — The wrong nuclear charge: containment is blind, delta is not
nodes.norm_label: figure 9.1 — the wrong nuclear charge: containment is blind, delta is not
nodes.rationale: Three-panel research figure arguing that the containment/bracket test is insensitive to an incorrect nuclear charge Z, while the quantum defect delta is a sharp discriminant. Left panel: bar chart of cells bracketed, 4/4 for both Z = 1 and Z = 2, annotated 'the bracket cannot see it'. Middle panel (red, labelled 'Z = 1 (wrong)'): delta rises near-linearly with n from about 2.65 at n = 4 to about 5.15 at n = 9, annotated 'spread 2.48'. Right panel (blue, labelled 'Z = 2 (correct)'): delta falls smoothly from about 1.308 at n = 4 to about 1.265 at n = 9, annotated 'spread 0.04'. Conclusion: flatness of delta across n, not bracket success, detects the wrong Z.

nodes.label: Bracket blindness: containment is insensitive to a wrong Z
nodes.norm_label: bracket blindness: containment is insensitive to a wrong z
nodes.rationale: Central claim of the figure's title. A containment criterion that both hypotheses satisfy carries no discriminating information; passing the bracket is therefore necessary but not sufficient, and a second, spread-based check is required.

nodes.label: Delta-flatness across n as diagnostic
nodes.rationale: The method the figure demonstrates: fit delta at each n under a candidate Z and measure its spread. A spread of 2.48 (Z = 1) versus 0.04 (Z = 2) — roughly a factor of 60 — separates the hypotheses cleanly where the bracket count does not.

nodes.rationale: The Challenge as documented (four-way triangulation, every source citing Loewdin 1969) demands ab initio with no fitted or empirical input, and Hartree-Fock is inside it; no source states an exactness or non-relativistic clause. Under (a) criterion 5 is met by the chain as it stands, but (a) rests on triangulation and Loewdin 1969 is still [SECONDARY] and paywalled.

nodes.label: Standard (b) — M's standard: an approximation cannot be a true derivation
nodes.community_name: recovered: The gap list G1–G5, all gating T4
nodes.norm_label: standard (b) — m's standard: an approximation cannot be a true derivation
nodes.rationale: M's standard: an approximation cannot be a true derivation. Under it no HF chain can meet criterion 5 at any amount of further work, because L3 is a variational restriction by construction; only the FCI limit meets it. The separation between (a) and (b) has been unresolved since s70 and is the only thing between the project and T4.

nodes.norm_label: al i 3s^2 54f (level carrying the tightest bound)
nodes.rationale: Neutral aluminium, a high-f Rydberg member. The annotation text is rendered small and set tight: it reads 'Al I 3s²54f', which parses as core 3s^2 plus a 54f Rydberg electron, but the split between the superscript 2 and the principal number 54 is not typographically separated in the figure, so '3s^2 5 4f' cannot be excluded from the pixels alone (AMBIGUOUS). Its Z=1 species label is consistent with the point sitting on the Z=1 envelope.

nodes.label: Scatter of 1,061 perturbation bounds
nodes.rationale: Small dark/blue markers so densely packed they read as a line. The count 1,061 is asserted in the title only; the markers cannot be counted from the rendered figure, so the cardinality is taken on the title's word (AMBIGUOUS as a reading of the plot itself).

nodes.label: Core charge Z as the family parameter
nodes.norm_label: core charge z as the family parameter

nodes.label: nu — effective principal quantum number (x-axis)
nodes.rationale: Logarithmic axis with a single decade tick at 10^1; data run from roughly nu = 2 to nu = 40. The axis is labelled only with the bare symbol nu — the figure never spells out that it is the effective principal quantum number, so that identification is read from the 2Z^2R/nu^3 scaling law rather than stated (AMBIGUOUS).

nodes.label: Upper bound on local perturbation (cm^-1)
nodes.rationale: The measured quantity, in wavenumbers, spanning roughly 1 cm^-1 to 3x10^5 cm^-1 across the plotted range. Smaller value = tighter constraint.

nodes.label: Reference curve 2Z^2R/nu^3 at Z = 1 (solid red)
nodes.rationale: Lower of the two envelopes, running from about 6x10^4 cm^-1 at nu ~ 2 down to about 1 cm^-1 near nu ~ 40. The bulk of the scatter lies on or immediately above this line — neutral, singly-charged-core behaviour.

nodes.label: Reference curve 2Z^2R/nu^3 at Z = 2 (dashed yellow)
nodes.rationale: Upper envelope, a factor of four above the Z=1 curve (Z^2 = 4), from about 2.5x10^5 cm^-1 at nu ~ 2 to about 4 cm^-1 at nu ~ 40. A sub-population of points tracks this line in the upper-left half of the plot, marking ionised species.

nodes.label: Rydberg constant R
nodes.rationale: Appears only inside the formula 2Z^2R/nu^3; its numerical value and units are never printed on the figure, though the cm^-1 y-axis implies the wavenumber form.

nodes.label: Scaling law 2Z^2R/nu^3
nodes.rationale: The hydrogenic local level spacing: twice the Rydberg energy scaled by charge squared over the cube of the effective quantum number. It sets the envelope the bounds must lie under, and its -3 log-log slope is what the scatter reproduces.

nodes.label: Tightest bound — 1.40 cm^-1
nodes.rationale: Called out with a filled red marker and a leader line at the low-bound, high-nu corner (nu of order 35-40). 'Tightest' means smallest: 1.40 cm^-1 is the strongest constraint any single passing cell places on a local perturbation.

nodes.label: Figure 16.1 — Every passing cell is a measurement: 1,061 perturbation bounds
nodes.norm_label: figure 16.1 — every passing cell is a measurement: 1,061 perturbation bounds
nodes.rationale: Log-log research figure. x-axis is the effective principal quantum number nu; y-axis is 'upper bound on local perturbation (cm^-1)'. A dense scatter of ~1,061 points falls on a straight descending line of slope -3 in log-log, bracketed by two analytic reference curves 2Z^2R/nu^3 for Z=1 (solid red) and Z=2 (dashed yellow). The demonstration: each cell of the index that passes the constraint yields a numerical upper bound on how large a local perturbation could be and still leave the cell passing, so a pass is not a null result but a measurement. The tightest (smallest) such bound in the set is annotated at 1.40 cm^-1 for Al I 3s^2 54f, sitting at the high-nu, low-bound end of the scatter.

nodes.label: Inverse-cube slope (nu^-3) of the bound envelope
nodes.norm_label: inverse-cube slope (nu^-3) of the bound envelope
nodes.rationale: Both reference curves and the whole scatter are straight and parallel on log-log axes with slope -3. The result the figure carries: the achievable bound is not scattered noise but is governed end-to-end by hydrogenic nu^-3 spacing, so the highest-nu cells are automatically the most constraining.

nodes.label: Every passing cell is a measurement
nodes.norm_label: every passing cell is a measurement
nodes.rationale: Design intent stated by the title: a cell that merely passes a constraint is normally read as no information. The figure argues the opposite — passing converts into a quantitative upper bound on any local perturbation, so the 1,061 passes are 1,061 measurements rather than 1,061 non-events.

nodes.label: Cap-independence of the generator pattern
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.rationale: Generator counts grow 17, 23, 31, 32 across six settings while fifteen patterns hold; only multiplicities change, which licenses stating the poset once.

nodes.label: Distributivity of Λ
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.rationale: Λ is a sublattice of a product of chains, so distributivity is forced; it is the least surprising and most load-bearing fact because it admits Birkhoff's representation.

nodes.label: Rank conservation (modularity), 475,800 pairs, zero violations
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.rationale: Modular equality is strictly stronger than the submodularity of matroid rank or entropy; it is the signature of distributivity and is a cheaper pairwise test, so it is run first.

nodes.label: Rank asymmetry — centre of mass 11.07 against midpoint 11.5
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.norm_label: rank asymmetry — centre of mass 11.07 against midpoint 11.5
nodes.rationale: There are more caps than floors, so the top is pruned harder; the skew measures how much more Pauli constrains than counting does.

nodes.label: d(x, x) = 1 — a point counts itself
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.norm_label: d(x, x) = 1 — a point counts itself
nodes.rationale: Not a convention: a point has no volume but is one occupied cell, and the measure counts occupied cells.

nodes.label: An interval bounds where something already is
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.norm_label: an interval bounds where something already is
nodes.rationale: An interval carries less than the coordinates do, not more, so the method returns a bound on a known location and never proposes an unlisted cell.

nodes.label: Transfer condition — void-free unit hypercube
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.rationale: Lattice and arithmetic Möbius values agree iff the interval is a void-free unit hypercube: 60 void-free pairs agree, 56 void-bearing disagree, no mixed case.

nodes.label: The occupancy measure d(x, y) = τ(lcm/gcd)
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.norm_label: the occupancy measure d(x, y) = τ(lcm/gcd)
nodes.rationale: The coordinate orders are partial and share only 0.3% of pairs, but every pair has a meet and a join, so the interval is total where the order is partial — that is why d is defined where no order relates x to y.

nodes.label: Prime encoding N(x) = ∏ pᵢ^{xᵢ}
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.rationale: Assigning the i-th coordinate the i-th prime makes Λ a sublattice of the divisor lattice of one integer, so order, join and meet become divisibility, lcm and gcd exactly rather than by analogy.

nodes.label: The cap convention (n,e,ℓ,k,f)_max = (3, 3, 1, 3, 1)
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.rationale: Λ has no natural end, so every count is taken at fixed finite caps; a cap-dependent figure naming no caps is at these caps, and the fault would be a figure at other caps that does not say so.

nodes.label: The counts move with the caps; the shape does not
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.norm_label: the counts move with the caps; the shape does not
nodes.rationale: Claims about shape are checked at several settings so nothing rests on where the counting happened to stop.

nodes.label: Moved from old §8.0 to front matter
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.norm_label: moved from old §8.0 to front matter
nodes.rationale: It applies from the first cap-dependent number (Chapter 4's counts), so it belongs at the front rather than in a later chapter; the self-audit around it is cut per the standing rule.

nodes.label: Standing rule — sketch in the main volume, full expansion in the compendium
nodes.community_name: drive: Rewrite — Chapter 6, “What Λ is — dist
nodes.norm_label: standing rule — sketch in the main volume, full expansion in the compendium
nodes.rationale: The main volume stays readable and the work stays fully proven; where an expansion does not yet exist it is flagged for authoring rather than left as if the sketch were the whole proof.

nodes.label: The Method 1.6 corpus checkout
nodes.rationale: Produced by chat 149 on 2026-09-02 so the corpus could be indexed by Graphify and reached from a repository checkout instead of being re-downloaded and re-extracted from Drive at the top of every chat; the .py members are the point, because a symbol and its blast radius become graph-queryable instead of requiring a 7.6 MB extraction.

nodes.label: Drive remains the store
nodes.rationale: The chat-68 ruling, restated chat 74 and by M in chat 147: this repository is an index and a convenience, never a second source of truth. When the two disagree, Drive wins and this tree is stale — regenerate it, do not repair it.

nodes.label: The `* -text` end-of-line rule
nodes.rationale: Without it a checkout on another platform would silently change every member's md5 and every round-trip guard would fail.

nodes.label: The standing member extraction regex
nodes.rationale: Extraction used `^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>\n` with re.S|re.M on the decoded bytes (CLAUDE.md §9), decoded with validate=True (G0e), into a single flat members/.

nodes.label: Regenerating after a new build
nodes.rationale: The tree is disposable. After the next close.py produces BUILD180+, rebuild from the new bundle rather than patching members, and let the round-trip guard prove the result.

nodes.label: The round-trip guard
nodes.rationale: The tree is not merely derived from the bundles; it reproduces them. Every member body was spliced back into the original bundle bytes at its recorded offset and the md5 of the result asserted, so a checkout of members/ is provably the extraction the §0 gate produces rather than an assertion that it is.

nodes.label: Fault F24.1 (record `it`; s23 rows unaudited)

nodes.label: v_gbz hard-cuts v_c where eps_c >= 0
nodes.rationale: The correlation potential is truncated where the correlation energy density turns non-negative; the cut is a known property of the form, not a bug.

nodes.label: FINDING-CELLCUT (SUBCELL cell-cut convergence)

nodes.community_name: recovered: Item 4 — The NIST ASD Species Files
nodes.rationale: Every number traces to a compilation, table and page, or to a database entry with its stated uncertainty; carried at channel level for all 153 channels.

nodes.label: D.2.2 Admissibility (r >= 5)
nodes.community_name: recovered: Item 4 — The NIST ASD Species Files
nodes.rationale: Levels must be separated by more than five times their uncertainty; r falls as nu^-3, so every channel eventually leaves the domain and the rule states where, in advance.

nodes.label: D.2.3 Cost Resolvability (nu <= nu_V)
nodes.community_name: recovered: Item 4 — The NIST ASD Species Files
nodes.rationale: The bracket needs levels separated; the cost needs curvature resolved, and curvature washes out first — so cells above nu_V are excluded from the cost test and retained for the bracket.

nodes.label: E.4 Computational Methods
nodes.community_name: recovered: Item 4 — The NIST ASD Species Files
nodes.rationale: Python 3 with NumPy; closure tests either exhaustive over all pairs or on uniform random samples with the sample size reported; Ritz fits by OLS on delta against 1/n^2 with the leverage term carried in sigma.

nodes.label: Quotation Granularity q
nodes.community_name: recovered: Item 4 — The NIST ASD Species Files
nodes.rationale: Read from the source table as the smallest nonzero increment appearing in it — 1e-3 cm-1 for most ASD entries, coarsening to 0.1 or 1 cm-1 in high-n regions — and it enters nu_V directly.

nodes.label: B-d — First r_l Cost-Domain Exit on Real Data
nodes.community_name: recovered: Item 4 — The NIST ASD Species Files
nodes.norm_label: b-d — first r_l cost-domain exit on real data
nodes.rationale: For an ion dT along l = 2 Z_eff^2 R d(delta)/nu^3, giving r_l = 395/(nu^3 sigma) at Z_eff=3; at sigma=0.05 cm-1 this exits below r_l=5 at nu ~ 11.7, so if the Be II f and g series reach n >~ 12 the pair leaves the cost domain inside its measured range.

nodes.rationale: Chosen over "an equation connecting two points" because the orders are partial and share only 0.3%; an interval is total, since every pair of cells has a meet and a join. Thm 11.2 permits it (an interval carries less than the coordinates), §18.6 permits it (a bound on where something already is, not a proposal about an unlisted cell), and the near-disjointness of the two intervals per pair makes what a thing IS and what it can BECOME separately bounded. It also explains the title: an equation returns a value, this returns an interval plus a verdict on what the interval is about, which is not expressible as an equation.

nodes.label: EQUATION chains read as all members equal
nodes.norm_label: equation chains read as all members equal
nodes.rationale: Pairing only the first = with what follows reads the second expression as a scalar and manufactures defects: MC §10.3's chain is one claim with three members, all 976, and read pairwise it looks like two defects and is neither.

nodes.label: NOT-BOUND — a fraction and a percentage the text does not bind
nodes.norm_label: not-bound — a fraction and a percentage the text does not bind
nodes.rationale: An assertion, not a result: 175 of 235 reader-facing claims are NOT-BOUND. 311/311 is 100% and the 57% beside it belongs to a different quantity, so a tool that paired them would report a defect that is not there.

nodes.label: ROUNDING-SENSITIVE — the tool never picks the convention for you
nodes.norm_label: rounding-sensitive — the tool never picks the convention for you
nodes.rationale: 1 of 8 = 13% is 13 under HALF_UP and 12 under HALF_EVEN, and which one the text meant is not the tool's to decide.

nodes.label: It commits large binaries automatically, with no review
nodes.norm_label: it commits large binaries automatically, with no review
nodes.rationale: Git history is expensive to undo — a file cannot be shrunk out by deleting it in a later commit; the size guard stops only the single case GitHub hard-rejects and nothing stops steady growth.

nodes.label: Ships dispatch-only; the schedule is commented out
nodes.norm_label: ships dispatch-only; the schedule is commented out
nodes.rationale: A scheduled run is never a dry run: it syncs for real and pushes a commit, and always uses the default branch's copy of the file.

nodes.label: Never passes --prune
nodes.rationale: Drive deletions are reported in the job log, not applied: a scheduled job that can delete committed files with no review is the unsafe default.

nodes.label: Manifest/tree bijection invariant
nodes.rationale: Exact bijection holds across the two mirrored root folders only, not everything under drive/: drive/chats/ is the sharded export, has no manifest rows, and --prune walks only the mirrored roots so it neither deletes nor demands rows for it.

nodes.label: The Forty-Eight Errors (Chapter 18)
nodes.rationale: Not forty-eight different mistakes but one mistake forty-eight times: the conclusion written before the output was read, sometimes with the contradicting numbers on the same printed line.

nodes.label: The Wrong Nuclear Charge (Chapter 9)
nodes.rationale: The bracket held 56 of 56 and could not notice, because Z cancels from containment; two quantities the method never uses were loud immediately. The object found the error because it carried more than it needed.

nodes.label: D.2.12 Withdrawal
nodes.rationale: Every retracted claim is logged with what replaced it; the register of forty-eight entries is the evidence for Chapter 9, not an apology for it.

nodes.label: D.2.13 Compute, Then Write
nodes.rationale: The protocol most often violated in the production of the book — prose asserting a conclusion while the contradicting output stands on the same screen — and stated because it is the one that most needed stating.

nodes.label: D.2.8 Two Independent Routes
nodes.rationale: D_def made operational: an identity computed along one path is vacuous — w = V*e cannot fail if V is defined as w/e. Realised experimentally in the antiprotonic-helium check where two laser measurements agree at 0.09 sigma with no shared step.

nodes.label: Isoelectronic Interpolation (1.3% median)
nodes.rationale: Quoted at 1.3% but used at the end of a sequence, where the measured cost is 2.1% for a hold-out and 3.5% for a genuine fifth member; the Sc VI route uses the last figure, not the first.

That is the entire gap and nothing else, and it is a spectral-gap/stability statement, i.e. Rung C.

nodes.rationale: The job condition tests the issue body and title rather than the event action, so assigning an issue whose text still says @claude would re-run an answered request — a duplicate reply and another ~508 MB checkout.

nodes.label: github.event.sender.type != 'Bot' guard
nodes.rationale: A cost control, not a safety one: the action already refuses bot actors, but only after paying for a ~508 MB checkout. The review workflow's own comments quote @claude and are exactly this case.

nodes.label: --allowedTools mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment
nodes.rationale: Required even though the skill's own frontmatter names the same tool: the action only starts the inline-comment MCP server when --allowedTools names it.

nodes.label: cancel-in-progress deliberately false on the review
nodes.norm_label: cancel-in-progress deliberately false on the review
nodes.rationale: The job is read-only to git but posts inline comments as it works; cancelling leaves a partial review, and the skill skips any PR that already carries a Claude comment, so every later run would skip and strand a truncated review forever. Queuing costs one cheap self-skipping run; cancelling costs correctness.

nodes.label: Three gates: fork, drive-only, missing key
nodes.norm_label: three gates: fork, drive-only, missing key
nodes.rationale: Skip cleanly rather than fail red on a condition the PR author cannot fix — a missing one-time setup step reported as if the PR were broken.

nodes.label: Interactive mode — no prompt input, so Claude waits to be mentioned
nodes.norm_label: interactive mode — no prompt input, so claude waits to be mentioned
nodes.rationale: Adding a prompt input would flip the action into automation mode, which runs unprompted.

nodes.label: Concurrency declared at job level, not workflow level
nodes.norm_label: concurrency declared at job level, not workflow level
nodes.rationale: Workflow-level concurrency is arbitrated at run-creation time, before the if: is evaluated, so ordinary comments would join the group and evict a queued real request. A job skipped by if: never queues. cancel-in-progress stays false because Claude may be mid-edit or mid-push.

nodes.label: github_token deliberately not passed
nodes.rationale: Omitting it authenticates as the Claude GitHub App; passing secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN would mean CI does not run on commits Claude pushes.

nodes.label: trigger_phrase alone is not enough
nodes.rationale: The job if: hardcodes the literal @claude in four places and runs before the action, so changing only the action input means the workflow never starts. Change both, or neither.

nodes.rationale: ν = n − a·v[p] is a linear functional, so the entrant is minimal for some a exactly when it is a vertex of the lower convex hull; each straddling chord is linear in v, hence the feasible set is a convex polyhedral cone with five irredundant chord facets plus seven monotonicity constraints.

nodes.rationale: The register compendium is only for subject-matter entries, a show of thought process and proof of work; all reader-perspective audits and editorial entries are forbidden from the books as irrelevant to any reader.

nodes.label: The Method 1.6 Working Register (editorial)
nodes.rationale: Established chat 12 under Ruling 27. Not a volume, never printed, never cited by any book — it exists so editorial findings have a home outside the reader-facing register.

nodes.label: The Constraint Graph is a Tree
nodes.norm_label: the constraint graph is a tree

nodes.label: Local E = 0 on Every Slice (new invariant)
nodes.norm_label: local e = 0 on every slice (new invariant)
nodes.rationale: Every A_q and B_q is closed under meet and join with E = 0 across all 8 slices and all q — closure holds locally, not only globally.

nodes.rationale: No standalone numeric of its own; anchored on the tree fact from MC-21 and box=cylinder from MC-18, so it is measured downstream rather than directly.

nodes.label: MC-18 §12.6.1 Two-Body Separation
nodes.rationale: Bare product 33*17*4 = 2,244 against the conditioned sum 165+330+345+136 = 976 exact — the conditioning is what recovers the lattice count.

nodes.label: MC-20 §12.8 Cross-Sections
nodes.rationale: Peak fibre 345 at q=2 is 35.3% of 976; the sequence 165,330,345,136 is log-concave hence unimodal; the 8->3 compression S(1,1,1) still counts 976.

nodes.label: MC-21 §12.9 Interval-is-Box, Antichains, Chains
nodes.rationale: 31,604 of 115,162 comparable intervals are boxes (27.4%, the book's '27%'); widest antichain 122 at rank 11 with 8 x 122 = 976; maximal chains 1,113,045,672 exact; chain length 17 equals 17 join-irreducibles — 'the two seventeens are one'.
